lines.text: Why do things fall down, instead of floating away?
Gravity is a force that pulls every object with mass toward every other object.
The more mass something has, the stronger its pull.
Earth is so massive that it pulls everything toward its center.
That's why people on the other side of the planet don't fall off.
Drop anything, and it speeds up by nine point eight meters per second, every single second.
Isaac Newton realized that the force pulling an apple down, also keeps the Moon in orbit.
Without air, a hammer and a feather fall at exactly the same speed.
He showed that mass bends space and time, and objects simply follow the curve.
So you're never really pulled down. You're just following the curve of space.
